technology noun

also tech, technical know-how

classical

Gell. 10.12.9
M-O s.v. technology

disciplīna mēchanica, disciplīnae mēchanicae f.

the science of machines and devices; technology

Gellius’s phrase for the art by which Archytas made a wooden dove fly; Morgan–Owens gives it for technology. Mēchanicus is ante-classical and post-Augustan (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • artēs mēchanicae, artium mēchanicārum f. pl. — the mechanical arts, technology

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. technology

    Morgan–Owens also allows artēs māchinālēs or fabrīlēs.

  • ars technica, artis technicae f. — technology

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. technology, after Egger

    Egger also writes technica disciplīna (Morgan–Owens).

Examples

  • simulācrum columbae ē lignō ab Archȳtā ratiōne quādam disciplīnāque mēchanicā factum volāsse

    that a model of a dove made of wood by Archytas, by a certain method and mechanical skill, flewGell. 10.12.9

See also computer, science, machine.

SourcesLewis & Short: mechanicus · Lewis & Short: disciplina · Lewis & Short: ars · Lewis & Short: technicus

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. technology.

Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-gellius), checked against the editions named there.

Traupman has no word for technology; he gives māchinālis scientia for engineering (pp. 166, 310).
